items.text: For one incident these counts describe this investigation only. They are not rates, trends or a benchmark.

308 of the 436 findings (70.6%) sit at levels 3 and 4: 167 at supervision and 141 at organisational influences, against 92 at preconditions and 36 unsafe acts. The largest rows are Supervision Inadequate (25 top-rated, 51 other) and Organisational Climate/ Culture Influences (19 top-rated, 32 other).

sections.heading: Latent conditions
sections.intro: Each condition runs under several separate findings and register learnings. The counts show how widely the investigation found it, not how much it contributed.

items.lesson: High-consequence work went ahead without written guidance, because no one had written the specification, procedure or criteria the work needed.
items.explanation: Missing policy and guidance from supervision (SVI 1.4) recurs in 21 findings, more than any other code. The gaps include the substitute gasket specification [EVD-8645], a return-to-service procedure for the high-pressure meter [EVD-2894], automatic shutdown from gas detection [EVD-8657] and the emergency plan's isolation criteria [EVD-4052]. The same code sits under 12 register learnings, including LR-01, LR-02 and LR-07.

items.lesson: Risks the site knew about were accepted as normal working, so unsafe conditions became the way tasks were done.
items.explanation: A culture that allowed unsafe tasks (OIC 2.1) has 36 links out, the most of any code, and appears in 14 of the 25 register learnings. It covers locally bought O-rings as a regular practice [EVD-8645], gas detection that only displayed an alarm [EVD-3452], isolation valves with no remote operation [EVD-3932] and a damaged flameproof lamp left in service [EVD-6916].

items.lesson: Repeat failures of the same seal were handled as routine repairs, so the warning they gave never reached a reliability review.
items.explanation: Inconsistent risk management (OIC 2.7) recurs in 19 findings and has 24 links out; the maintenance, spares and support programme (OIR 1.6) has 26 links out. Both meet at meter 310FT01: three gasket replacements in about 22 months were not escalated for root-cause action [EVD-1494] [EVD-0591].

items.lesson: The change procedure existed on paper but was not in use, so a material substitution on a pressure boundary had no change review.
items.explanation: The 2016 management-of-change procedure had not been used since 2018 [EVD-2986]. The same condition is coded four ways: missing guidance (SVI 1.4), a culture that allowed unsafe tasks (OIC 2.1), inconsistent risk management (OIC 2.7) and a problem left uncorrected (SVF 3.2).

items.lesson: Integrity findings that were measured and reported stayed open for years without a corrective plan.
items.explanation: The Failure to Correct Known Problem row holds 40 findings; operations management (SVF 3.2) recurs 18 times and ineffective action against an identified risk (SVF 3.4) 14 times. The 2017 thickness survey had no corrective plan three years later [EVD-5527], and pitted pipe on a zero-corrosion-allowance line was painted [EVD-2397].

sections.heading: What this profile cannot tell you

items.text: The counts show how often the investigation coded a factor and how often a causal explanation named a link. They do not measure how much a factor contributed: one condition is often coded several ways, as the change procedure is above, and a link counts mentions, not strength. The ratings are the investigation's own. Nothing here compares this site with another site or with an earlier year.

gaps.text: The export cannot show whether the same latent conditions exist at other sites, because it covers one incident.
gaps.evidence_needed: Findings from other investigations coded on the same HFACS framework, or an audit of the same conditions at other sites.

limits: A desk analysis of the published enquiry report: no site access, interviews or records beyond it.
The feeds and recurrence tables show their first 12 rows; the full lists are in hfacs_profile.json.
